clue.text: Black bird dog

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark-feathered bird and a hound, listed side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' reads as a blackbird, but the colour supplies a single letter and the bird is a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hunting hound breed, a specific example of a dog.

clue.text: Some Chablis — sufficient will bring perfect happiness

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only a portion of the run of letters written out in the clue

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the wine and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Enough Chablis wine is all it takes to make someone utterly content.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is a state of complete joy, a synonym for perfect happiness.

clue.text: A speech holding duke in high regard

indicators.note: something holding another thing keeps it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: An address that holds a nobleman up as deeply esteemed.
explanation.walkthrough: The duke sits inside 'A speech', just after the A: A + D + ORATION gives ADORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and esteem, a stronger synonym for holding someone in high regard.

clue.text: Stage turn's mild deception

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
to turn or wrench something can be to pull it, as with a pulled muscle

explanation.surface: An actor's routine on stage is just a gentle trick on the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests the theatre, but here it means one section of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a teasing joke or hoax, a playful and harmless kind of deception.

clue.text: Following Carole abroad, two females go away

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the name taken as letters to rearrange
F is the abbreviation for female, twice

explanation.surface: Two women trail after Carole on her foreign trip, then head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the two Fs after the rearranged name; it joins pieces and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off is an informal phrasal verb meaning to leave or depart, matching go away.

clue.text: Pub licence obtained from council

parts.note: a local is a person's regular neighbourhood pub
a licence is authority or permission to do something

explanation.surface: A pub must get its drinks licence from the council.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the local council grants pub licences, so the surface is literally true; 'the local' is British slang for one's usual pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a council is the local authority, the elected body running an area's services.

clue.text: Kindly, a fellow in allegory

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a fable is a moral tale, a kind of allegory

explanation.surface: A kindly character appears in an allegorical tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply run one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and good-natured, so it can replace the adjective kindly.

clue.text: Duck's grim smell

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O
dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: A duck gives off an unpleasant whiff.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a noun for a scent, usually unpleasant, the same as a smell.

clue.text: Notion which brings an exclamation of surprise

parts.note: a fancy is a whim or notion
that and which are both relative pronouns

explanation.surface: An idea that makes someone gasp in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: "Fancy that!" is a stock expression of mild astonishment, an interjection of surprise.

clue.text: Shocking union, a seemingly unlikely coalition

parts.note: unholy can mean dreadful or outrageous, as in an unholy row
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: An outrageous partnership between two sides nobody expected to team up.
explanation.definitionFit: An unholy alliance is an idiom for a pact between parties who would normally be opponents.

clue.text: Man-made can, origin uncertain

indicators.note: something uncertain is unsettled, so the letters have no fixed order yet

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: An artificial tin can whose source is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic means not derived from living matter, so artificial or synthetic rather than natural.

clue.text: Loud argument before noon could make one scowl

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a row is a noisy quarrel
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A shouting match before midday is enough to put anyone in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places the argument ahead of the noon letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to wrinkle the brow in displeasure, a near synonym of the verb scowl.

clue.text: Landmark built free, to stay at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all four words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A monument constructed to remain standing offshore, free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the real statue, which stands on an island in New York Harbor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty is a famous New York monument, an example of a landmark.

clue.text: Passageway in pretty empty Scottish town

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A corridor in an attractive but deserted Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is a large town west of Glasgow, also famous for the teardrop fabric pattern.

clue.text: With farming implement, boy makes laborious progress

parts.note: a plough turns over soil in a field
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A farm lad works his way slowly across a field with a plough.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read PLOUGH + SON, regrouped as PLOUGHS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough on is an idiom for continuing doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: Find seven letters in bureau near this

indicators.note: a fixed count of letters lying inside the following words tells the solver to look within them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across into the third

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint: there are seven letters to find in a desk near here.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up or discover, so it can stand for the verb find.

clue.text: Ice, mostly, on top of old Irish lake

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: reserve is cool, icy formality of manner
O is the abbreviation for old
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Ice sitting on an ancient Irish lough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' means frostiness of manner, not frozen water. In a down clue 'on top of' puts the shortened word above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake used to store a water supply.

clue.text: Personal objective in a move that backfired?

parts.note: one's own means belonging personally to oneself
a goal is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A private aim pursued through a plan that went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal is figuratively any action that harms its doer; in football it is scoring for the opposition.

clue.text: Cicero's art in prayer room

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the craft of public speaking, at which the Roman Cicero excelled
second meaning: a small chapel for private worship

explanation.surface: The Roman statesman practising his rhetoric in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both eloquent public speaking and a small chapel set aside for prayer.

clue.text: Worker fixed part of phone

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: An engineer repaired a component of a telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' reads as repaired, but it means firm or settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The handset is the receiver of a telephone, the piece held to the ear.

clue.text: Position of gear in Renault, idling?

indicators.note: the question mark lets idling suggest the letters are loose and out of order, not set to work

parts.note: the car make taken as letters

explanation.surface: Which gear a Renault car is in while its engine idles.
explanation.walkthrough: A car left idling is usually in neutral, so the surface is true as well as cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gear setting where the engine is disengaged from the wheels.

clue.text: Soldiers disregard an urge to change

indicators.note: asking the letters to change means they must be reordered

parts.note: all three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Troops ignore their impulse to alter course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadier Guards are a British Army infantry regiment, known for ceremonial duty at Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Owned liberal supply

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are given freedom of order

parts.note: taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone possessed a generous stock of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal supply' reads as a generous quantity, but 'supply' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide or furnish someone with something, so it works as the verb supply.

clue.text: Girl locked up in prison, a suspect

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top
locked in means held inside, so the letters sit within the clue's words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A woman jailed as a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a woman's first name, and crosswords often define names as girl.

clue.text: Nerdy type, unhappy attending party

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A geek turning up glum at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddo is British slang for a socially inept or pathetic person, close to a nerd.

clue.text: Film noir, too gruesome — American

indicators.note: something gruesome is mangled and horrible, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: letters of the two words to rearrange
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A film critic finds a noir movie too gory, and American at that.
explanation.walkthrough: Notorious is a 1946 Hitchcock film, fittingly American and close to noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious is the title of Hitchcock's 1946 thriller, an example of a film.

clue.text: Bride from Welwyn confused journalist

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the place name taken as letters
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporter muddles up a story about a bride from Welwyn.
explanation.walkthrough: Welwyn is a town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride is a woman just married or about to be, so she is a newlywed.

clue.text: Old coin German boy brought back home

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Rolf is a German boy's name
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A German lad brings an antique coin home with him.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British two-shilling coin, withdrawn after decimalisation, so an old coin.
